content:
Marta P.: quick heads-up — I tried the console on a foldable in landscape and hit a couple UX oddities. sharing screenshots in thread. :eyes:
Devon (Design): thanks — saw that too. table rows collapse, the action chips (•••) are right on the hinge seam on smaller widths. taps are flaky.
Jordan (QA): repro steps: open dashboard > pods table > rotate to landscape on foldable emulator (inner width ~520px). rows wrap mid-cell, and action chip becomes inaccessible if it falls under seam.
Alex R. (Frontend): can you paste the exact viewport size? I want to reproduce locally.
Jordan (QA): emulator shows content-box width 520, safe-area-left 24, safe-area-right 24. effective tappable area drops to ~472px.
Sam K. (PM): main asks: 1) ensure table doesn't compress columns into unreadable lumps, 2) keep action controls fully tappable away from hinge, 3) avoid horizontal scrolling where possible unless explicit.
Devon (Design): proposed changes: - force wrap-to-stacked rows at <=560px so cells become stacked cards rather than forcing tiny columns. - move action chips to end-row overflow menu when width <600px. - increase hit area for chips to 44px min-touch target.
Alex R. (Frontend): implementation notes: prefer progressive enhancement — add breakpoint and a small layout switch:
```
/* layout guard for very narrow landscape / foldables */
@media (max-width: 560px) {
  .pods-table { display: block; }
  .pods-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 8px; }
  .row-actions { position: relative; margin-top: 6px; }
}
.action-chip { min-width: 44px; padding: 8px 10px; touch-action: manipulation; }
```
Alex R. (Frontend): alternatively we can keep table but force `overflow-x: auto` and sticky action column — downside: horizontal scroll on foldable seam which is annoying.
Devon (Design): I'd avoid horizontal scroll as primary solution. It's okay as fallback but stacked/compact-cards are friendlier on small landscape.
Marta P.: accessibility nit — when we change to stacked rows, ensure header labels are preserved visually for each stacked field (like key: value) not just invisible ARIA labels. Also make focus order consistent.
Jordan (QA): regression checklist: keyboard nav, screen reader readout for stacked rows, hit-target test (44px) for action chips, and rotate tests for seam. I'll add cases.
Sam K. (PM): decision proposal: implement stacked layout at <=560px, move actions into a single overflow menu for that mode, keep overflow-x:auto as fallback for legacy devices. Alex, estimate effort?
Alex R. (Frontend): ~2 dev-days + 1 QA day for tests + small design polish. Could aim for next sprint.
Devon (Design): will upload updated comps (stacked rows + overflow menu) and provide copy tweaks for the overflow label ("More actions") and accessible labels. Also recommend 16px tap margin around chips to reach 44px.
Marta P.: perfect. @Alex R. please add a feature flag so we can rollout to dedicated devices first. Jordan plz add regression tests. Devon, drop the comps link here when ready. :thumbsup:
design-bot: new mock uploaded: https://assets.redwood.internal/designs/foldable-stack-v2.png
Jordan (QA): added test ticket RF-4721 to test queue with steps and expected results.
Sam K. (PM): thanks everyone. follow-up: add a short console release note about foldable responsiveness and the action overflow behavior.
Devon (Design): small copy suggestion for overflow menu: change "More" to "Actions" for clarity.
Marta P.: agreed — "Actions" is clearer. closing for now, will reopen if QA finds more issues. :white_check_mark:
